seo_description: Free, open-source macOS menu bar app that tracks monthly internet usage against your data cap and warns you before you hit it. Native and private.
hero_sub: Set your monthly allowance and DataCapGuard keeps a live gauge in your menu bar, projects your month-end total, and warns you before you reach the cap.
features_sub: DataCapGuard does one job, tracking usage against your monthly cap, and keeps everything on your Mac.

features.title: Menu bar gauge
features.desc: Show a ring, a percentage, or both. The color shifts toward amber and red as your usage grows.

features.title: Projection and 30-day chart
features.desc: See used, left, projected and daily average, plus a Swift Charts bar chart of the last 30 days. The projection turns red if it would exceed your cap.

features.title: Warnings at your thresholds
features.desc: Get notified at 75, 90 and 100 percent by default, or pick your own. Each warning fires once per billing period.

features.title: Choose what gets counted
features.desc: Count all physical interfaces, Wi-Fi only, or Ethernet only. VPN and virtual interfaces are excluded by default to avoid double counting.

features.title: Hotspot mode
features.desc: Enter a network name such as your iPhone and only traffic on that network counts, so home usage never mixes in.

features.title: Reliable counting
features.desc: Samples every 5 seconds and right after wake, treats counter resets as a new baseline, and keeps daily totals across reboots. A manual adjustment lets you match your provider's meter.

permissions_step: When prompted, allow Notifications so DataCapGuard can warn you; Location access is optional and only needed for Hotspot mode to read your Wi-Fi name (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services).

faq.q: Is DataCapGuard really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, with no accounts, subscriptions or in-app purchases. The source is on GitHub, and there is an optional Support button if you want to chip in.

Notifications, so it can warn you at your thresholds; if you decline, it still tracks usage and shows a banner. Location is optional and only affects Hotspot mode, because macOS may hide the Wi-Fi name without it. It never asks for Accessibility, Screen Recording or Microphone access.
Only on your Mac. Daily usage totals are saved as a JSON file in Application Support, and the app reads per-interface byte counters, never the contents of your traffic. Nothing is sent to any server.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, which this free project does not have. Right-click the app and choose Open once to launch it, or build it from source with Xcode.
